• Valkyries host Dream in winner-take-all Game 7

Bryan will be here shortly. In the meantime here’s a look back at Thursday’s Game 6.

title: Atlanta Dream v Golden State Valkyries: WNBA finals 2026 Game 7 – live buildup

author: Giles Richards at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
description:
• George Russell second on grid after qualifying

  • Antonelli well placed as he nears title confirmation

Even as Formula One’s young gun Kimi Antonelli remains on course to claim his first world championship on Sunday it was the veteran, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton who gave a salutary reminder that there is very much fight left in the old dog yet as he claimed a spectacular pole position for the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Hamilton delivered a superb lap for Ferrari to secure his first pole for the team and just beat Mercedes’ George Russell into second. World champion in waiting Antonelli was in fourth place but remains in position to close out the title on Sunday, although Hamilton and Russell, who must win the race to have any hope of keeping the fight alive, have at least locked out the front row.
title: Lewis Hamilton storms to his first Ferrari pole at F1 Mexican GP with Antonelli fourth

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Prime minister says shake-up is vital to restore tribunal crippled by years of political disputes

Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, has vowed to see through a contested overhaul of the country’s constitutional court, declaring that “in certain matters, there can be no compromise”.

In a prime-time television address on Saturday night, Tusk was defiant, despite overnight protests that saw riot police drafted to protect the court’s building, saying the shake-up was vital to restore a tribunal crippled by years of political disputes.

Continue reading...
title: Tusk defends overhaul of Poland’s constitutional court despite protests

author: Lucy Mangan
description:
The Heated Rivalry actor plays two people in this genre-bending mystery. And Carrie-Anne Moss is fantastic as a horny author – who might have supernatural powers

Well, here’s an unexpected answer to the question of what Hudson Williams did next: the overnight megastar created by the smash-hit success of Heated Rivalry (hot young men bang each other for seven episodes, emotional connection also glossed, intermittent hockey scenes) appears as two characters in the spooky thriller Yaga.

Williams plays Henry Park, the missing scion of a powerfully rich family in the spooky Canadian coastal town of Whittock, and Henry’s spookily looky-likey roommate Logan, who lives in the Parks’ staffed mansion rent-free in return for helping Henry with his podcasts, parties and possible bisexuality. There is a lot of all three about these days among the young, I’m told. Usually by their podcasts.
title: Yaga review – this erotic witchy thriller starring Hudson Williams is a total head-messer

Portentous driver countdown time, with Hirakawa in there.

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Ruling ‘with prejudice’ means US president may not amend or refile his lawsuit over his alleged birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein

A US judge dismissed Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal with prejudice on Saturday, according to a court filing, bringing an end to his legal challenge over the newspaper’s reporting on his alleged birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein.

The decision follows an earlier dismissal in April that had allowed Trump to revise his complaint. As of Saturday, the case is dismissed with prejudice, meaning the lawsuit cannot be amended or refiled.

Continue reading...
title: Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein birthday letter

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Jewish groups welcome the new patrol unit in the wake of the Bondi terror attack. But experts say police use of long-arm firearms must be strictly controlled

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Police officers armed with military rifles are a familiar sight in some major global tourist destinations. Now, in an Australian first, they will be visible in Sydney too.

On Sunday, the New South Wales police launched a permanent special unit to patrol tourist areas, crowded public spaces, major events, sporting matches and places of worship – armed with military rifles.

Continue reading...
title: Some NSW police are now armed with military-style rifles. And they could be deployed to protests

author: Taha Hashim
description:
• Fakhar Zaman scores 127 from 99 balls in Lahore

  • Kamindu Mendis’s 131 proves in vain for Sri Lanka

This mini-tournament has been a welcome change of pace, carrying more meaning than your bog-standard three-match white-ball slog between two teams. And then there’s the gift of a final to crown the winners. This was an apt conclusion under lights in front of a packed-out Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore, settled in the penultimate over as Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by three wickets to win the tri-series.

Fakhar Zaman, Pakistan’s hero from the 2017 Champions Trophy final, was at the centre, crashing his way to 127 in a chase of 326. But plenty of work remained after his dismissal, and the new boys needed to stay calm. Arafat Minhas, 21, and Hasan Nawaz, 24, played it like old-timers, their partnership of 94 securing the game. Minhas and Faheem Ashraf fell with two runs still required, but Shaheen Afridi finished the evening with a wallop over the ropes
title: Pakistan win tri-series final as Fakhar Zaman century denies Sri Lanka in thrilling chase

author: Jacob Steinberg at Stamford Bridge
description:
• Defeat against Chelsea extends winless run to nine games

  • Carrick clinging on to job after club’s worst run since 1988

Michael Carrick insisted he would still be in charge when Manchester United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, despite the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday. United’s problems mounted as their winless run reached nine games. Carrick is clinging on to his job after overseeing the club’s first such run since 1988 and tried to focus on the next game as he analysed his side’s defending when Morgan Rogers opened the scoring for Chelsea.

“It’s never a good goal to concede,” he said. “Morgan went through the middle of us and at that point the game was right in the balance. To concede like that was a big moment. I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now.”
title: Michael Carrick insists he will still be in charge of Manchester United against Roma

author: Chris Hippensteel (now)
description:
This is already nearly five million more votes than the total number of early votes made in the last midterm elections, in 2022

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US email

A planned campaign event between Abdul El-Sayed, Michgan’s Democratic nominee for Senate, and Haley Stevens, his erstwhile primary opponent, appears in jeopardy after a renewed feud between the two.

Jason Turkish, Stevens’ fiance, was asked on Fox News on Saturday morning whether Stevens would go ahead with the appearance tomorrow.

Continue reading...
title: Early midterm voting surges with more than 50m ballots cast so far – live

author: Lauren Cochrane
description:
Gap, M&S, Topshop and more are taking a leaf from luxury label playbooks to satisfy savvier generation of shoppers

High street brands that boomed in the noughties before the squeeze of both sustainably minded consumers and the rise of ultra-cheap online labels are staging a comeback.

This time, rather than focusing solely on trend-led affordable designs, the names familiar to any shopper are courting luxury fashion, A-list collaborations and enhanced services in an attempt to engage consumers.

Continue reading...
title: A-listers and AI stylists: how high-street brands are staging a fashion comeback

author: Chris Stein in Unalaska, Alaska
description:
On the Bering Sea, Unalaska is the US’s most productive seafood port, employing thousands of workers. But Trump’s cuts, and his disastrous war with Iran, have caused chaos – and put Republican control of Congress at risk

It was less than 17 hours until the start of Alaska’s lucrative Bering Sea crab season, and Oystein Lone was standing on a dock in the city of Unalaska, preparing to embark in rough conditions.

The problem wasn’t the next day’s forecast of 60mph gusts, which would kick up white-capped swells and make crabbing, already one of the most dangerous jobs in the United States, even more hazardous. Nor was it the question of whether there’d be enough red king, tanner and snow crabs to go around – state regulators had, in fact, announced higher quotas for the season.
title: It’s closer to Beijing than Washington – and residents of this Alaskan outpost are reeling from Trump’s policies

author: Ariana Baio
description:
But select Democrats, too, are being accused of having ties to the late sex offender as country prepares to vote

In races across the country, Democratic candidates or groups that support them have released ads accusing Republicans of protecting pedophiles by voting against legislation to release files related to Jeffrey Epstein.

The ads appear intended to evoke an emotional response by accusing candidates of “protecting” Epstein, a notorious pedophile accused of running a sex-trafficking ring involving minors.

Continue reading...
title: Ads accusing Republican candidates of protecting Epstein fill airwaves in final midterm push

author: Jacob Steinberg at Stamford Bridge
description:
Get ready for another week of agonising over the sorry state of Manchester United. The legends of old will rage, clips of a fuming Gary Neville will fly around social media, the airwaves will reverberate with complaints from angry supporters and by the time United play again there is every chance a new manager will be in the dugout.

There were echoes of Erik ten Hag’s final game in charge as the walls closed in on Michael Carrick at Stamford Bridge. United missed a series of golden chances when the scores were level, just as they did when Ten Hag lost to West Ham a day before his sacking two years ago, and Chelsea made the most of the reprieve after initially delivering a performance so bad it had you worrying for the nascent Xabi Alonso project.

Continue reading...
title: Manchester United crisis deepens with Chelsea defeat and Martínez red card

author: Sammy Gecsoyler
description:
Police start arresting demonstrators with Met commander alleging they are ‘essentially meeting to purposefully commit a crime’

Police have started making arrests at the first mass demonstration under Andy Burnham’s premiership opposing the proscription of Palestine Action.

More than 100 people gathered outside the US embassy in Battersea, south London, holding signs that read: “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action.”

Continue reading...
title: More than 100 protest against Palestine Action ban outside US embassy in London

author: Aamna Mohdin Community affairs correspondent
description:
Nigerian care worker Kolade says he was left in tears after being excluded from talks with Shabana Mahmood over proposed changes to immigration system

Kolade had carefully prepared what he would tell the home secretary about the elderly people he cares for, the life his family had built in Britain and how her immigration proposals could threaten both.

The meeting with Shabana Mahmood had already been rescheduled twice. When the third date fell during a holiday, he cut his trip short to travel to London. But hours before the meeting was due to take place, it was cancelled after Mahmood declined to allow him to attend.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Was I not enough?’: care worker barred from meeting home secretary

author: Shakira Hussein
description:
Shakira Hussein’s concerns about her bipolar diagnosis were dismissed as common among ‘women like you’. Then she was found to have MS

In the five years since her diagnosis with multiple sclerosis, the Emmy award-winning actor Christina Applegate has become a prominent spokesperson for people living with the neurological disease. Both her memoir, published earlier this year, and the MS-themed podcast MeSsy that she co-hosts with fellow actor Jamie Lynn Sigler have significantly raised public awareness about multiple sclerosis and the broader topic of living with disability.

So Applegate’s recent revelation that her neurologist now believes that she does not have the disease after all came as a shock to me and to many other people living with multiple scleros
title: Christina Applegate’s multiple sclerosis misdiagnosis is not an isolated event. I should know | Shakira Hussein

author: Sam Levine
description:
The administration’s efforts have raised concerns among experts about potential disruptions after election day

Donald Trump is waging a brazen effort to interfere with voting in this year’s midterm elections, escalating concerns that the federal government will try to slow down certification of election results – a strategy that could create chaos when the new Congress is seated next year.

Experts are certain the administration’s efforts to subvert America’s elections will not work. And some have bemoaned “fearmongering” about far-fetched scenarios that are unlikely to go anywhere in court.

Continue reading...
title: How Trump and his allies seek to interfere the US midterm elections

author: Tiago Rogero in Brasília
description:
There are many explanations for the incumbent president’s win over Flávio Bolsonaro, but analysts – and he – point to reinvention of his social media use

Four days before his stunning electoral comeback, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil’s president, got his first smartphone.

Lula, who turned 81 last Tuesday, had long said he wanted to avoid an endless stream of calls during his rare moments off, and he began his presidential campaign by sticking to an old habit: using aides’ phones – only when necessary.

Continue reading...
title: The secret behind Lula’s win in Brazil may be an ‘army’ – of social media creators

author: Rob Evans, Harry Davies,Louisa Loveluck and Emine Sinmaz
description:
According to documents obtained by the Guardian, officials accused Cambridgeshire force of breaching US-UK deal by handing over case of woman strangled by US pilot

Ministry of Defence officials have privately accused a UK police force of wrongly handing over the investigation of an American fighter pilot who strangled a British woman to the US military, according to documents obtained by the Guardian.

Cambridgeshire police allowed the US military police to quickly take control of the investigation into Capt Jacob Wulfson after he had been accused of sexually assaulting Sarah Steele in his Cambridge flat.

Continue reading...
title: UK police should not have let US force take over airbase trial, MoD documents show

author: Hilary Beaumont
description:
Environmental Defense Fund analysis shows administration handed out $950m and Clean Air Act exemptions

It’s a good time to be a coal plant in the US. The Trump administration has given support to almost half of the nation’s coal plants, helping them to continue operating despite economic and regulatory headwinds, according to a new analysis by the Environmental Defense Fund.

The analysis, which looked at the 184 operating coal plants that are connected to the grid, found that 90 received support from the Trump administration through “cash handouts, free passes to pollute, and requirements to stay online past their retirement dates”.

Continue reading...
title: Trump boosted half of US coal plants with taxpayer dollars and ‘free passes to pollute’, report says

author: Eric Berger
description:
After canceling events in 2025, US cities including Henderson, Kentucky, are reviving public Day of the Dead events

Julia, a 19-year-old born in the US, and her parents, undocumented immigrants from Mexico, enjoyed attending the Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) celebration each year in Henderson, Kentucky, and selling aguas frescas, horchatas and a sweet bread traditionally eaten on the Mexican holiday.

Last year, her family also built an ofrenda, or altar, featuring flowers and a violin, to honor her grandfather, who played the instrument and died in 2023 in Mexico.

Continue reading...
title: Día de los Muertos celebrations rise from the dead as ICE arrests continue: ‘It’s important to bring joy in dark times’

author: Arwa Mahdawi
description:
The first lady has been praised for ‘singlehandedly’ brokering a ceasefire in a Ukrainian city – though she might have had some help

Haters be damned: Donald Trump just keeps on winning. He won the inaugural Fifa peace prize last year and was presented with the completely real, totally not made-up “Man of the Century” award at a recent rally. The president has also spent the greater part of a decade claiming he was once crowned Michigan’s Man of the Year: a fantastic achievement considering there is no such award and Trump has never lived in Michigan.

But despite his many trophies, there is one honour that has proved elusive: the Nobel peace prize. Trump holds
title: Hear me out: maybe Norway should give Melania Trump the Nobel peace prize | Arwa Mahdawi

author: Kate Wyver
description:
Whether it’s immersive chiller Blackout or the campily scary 2:22: A Ghost Story, ‘tis the season to be scared witless at the theatre. But what’s the secret to making an audience gasp in terror?

It was 1am. Total darkness. Locking up a wedding venue, Sam Beech’s car sensor went off: there was something behind him. “It went on for half an hour,” the writer and director recalls, “on the front bumper, then round the back. But every time I looked, there was nothing.” It kept going, snuffling around the car. So he stopped looking. “I thought: ‘If I don’t look behind me, it won’t get me.’” Since then, Beech, the creator of one of a plethora of horror shows currently haunting the stage, admits, “I don’t like driving in the dark”.

Beech’s experience was eerily similar to a scene in Andy Nyman’s hit 2010 play Ghost Stories, which Beech had seen four times, so the gnarly end the character had
title: Jump scares, leather gloves and squeaking moth noises: theatre horror masters on how they make their shows so scary

author: Rebecca Nicholson
description:
His dashing lead role in Jilly Cooper’s bonkbuster didn’t hurt the actor’s pin-up status, but now, he protests, he’s 43 – and a dad

Aidan Turner has a tactical beard. For the last two decades or so, the actor has found himself in roles that have made him a smouldering pin-up. Audiences really love to look at him. You can buy mugs that say, “Today I don’t feel like doing anything … except Aidan Turner.” There are entire Reddit forums dedicated to sharing photographs of him looking hot. He knows this about himself, just like he knows that people want to ask him about it. “I do get asked these questions,” he says, a little wearily. “I do get the, you know, word ‘smoulder’ or ‘sexy’, and all that kind of shit.” So right now, he has a full beard, in the hope that he will not be accused of, for example, smouldering. “I thought it wouldn’t happen so much with the beard,” he sighs. “I thought I could get away with it. I was going for ‘dad’.”

The job of actor
title: ‘The sexy stuff has got to be coming to an end, right?’: Rivals star Aidan Turner on beards, ballroom dancing and putting Poldark to bed

author: George Francis Lee and Dan Milmo
description:
Almost 40% of British singles have used AI for romantic advice, from writing messages to assessing potential partners

After Sam’s ex joked that her sister found him ugly, he turned to AI. Google Gemini had a look at the photo and politely disagreed. AI has been his wingman ever since, aiding his dating life by giving pep talks and vetting his messages.

The 27-year-old from Stoke-on-Trent is not the only AI-assisted romantic – a survey of 3,000 British singles published this month by Match Group, the owner of the Tinder and Hinge platforms, found 39% had used AI in their dating lives.

Continue reading...
title: Is AI your new wingman? How chatbots are transforming dating

author: Sammy Gecsoyler
description:
UK chancellor’s plans add to concerns government is moving away from pro-renewables agenda

John Healey has said he will veto new offshore wind projects if they will not lower bills, adding to concerns that the government is moving away from the pro-renewables agenda.

Announcing his plans, the chancellor said clean power is “how we break the grip of international gas prices on our bills”, but added the shift towards it “has to come at the right pace, in the right places, with the grid to carry it”.

Continue reading...
title: Healey to veto new offshore wind projects if they will not lower bills

description:
⚽ Updates on the 12.30pm GMT kick-off in west London
⚽ Football Daily | Goalscorers | Live Scores | Email Scott

Both teams welcome back a fan favourite. Estevao starts for Chelsea, while Bruno Fernandes returns for Manchester United.

Chelsea: Penders, Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Palestra, Caicedo, Lavia, Neto, Palmer, Estevao, Rogers.

author: Jack Snape
description:
• Pool A: Kangaroos 66-6 Cook Islands in Townsville

  • Tom Trbojevic scores second hat-trick in as many games

Reece Walsh showed if there was anything James Tedesco could do, he can do better with a starring role for the Kangaroos in a partly clunky but otherwise entertaining victory over the Cook Islands in Townsville.

Coach Kevin Walters faces a choice between the two brilliant No 1s for the much-anticipated semi-final against either Samoa or Tonga next week, but this only sometimes convincing display showed there is still work to do in camp Kangaroo.

Continue read
title: Reece Walsh fires clunky Australia to Rugby League World Cup win against Cook Islands

author: Rachel Leingang, George Chidi, David Smith, Fabiola Cineas, Dani Anguiano and Ed Pilkington, with graphics by Andrew Witherspoon
description:
Days away from a national verdict on Trump 2.0, we check in with nine midterm voters across the US and the political spectrum

US voters will soon deliver a national verdict on the second presidency of Donald Trump. On 3 November, millions of Americans will vote in midterm elections to decide control of the House of Representatives and Senate, as well as the governorships in 36 states and state legislatures across the country. The results could have a huge impact on Trump’s final two years in office.

Our reporters have interviewed nine voters across the country and the political spectrum about extremism in US politics, their confidence in the US voting system, what they hope Congress will tackle first and their views of the president’s secretary of defense, Pete Hegseth.
title: Election integrity, extremism and Pete Hegseth: nine voters on the US midterm election

author: Grace Holliday
description:
It was very cold and the young smoker was barelegged, barefoot and wearing a fur coat … How could the photographer resist?

This Margate shop is now an ice-cream parlour, but back in 2014 it was a vintage clothes store. Mark McEvoy, who had relocated from London the previous year with his partner and baby daughter, approached the young woman to ask permission to take this shot.

“I remember it being a very cold October day, so I was surprised she was barelegged and barefoot,” he says. “My guess is that she was working in the shop, or maybe a friend of someone working there. The fur coat may even have been for sale inside, just something she put on to keep warm during a cigarette break.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘A gust of wind blowing back her hair added something special’: Mark McEvoy’s best phone picture

author: Jeremy Nguyen
description: Continue reading...
title: Jeremy Nguyen on a very arty pumpkin – cartoon

author: Norman Solomon
description:
The unprecedented measure has enormous potential nationwide. The clash exposes the party’s corporate-progressive divide

Midway through this summer, a high-quality poll found that Democrats in California were overwhelmingly in favor of the upcoming ballot measure for a one-time 5% tax on billionaire wealth.

The ratio was more than 4 to 1. But the state’s most powerful Democrats – including the governor Gavin Newsom, his near-certain successor Xavier Becerra and the Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass – have lined up with Silicon Valley billionaires who’ve raised upward of $340m to defeat the initiative.

Continue reading...
title: Top Democrats are fighting a billionaire tax in California. Their voters are on the other side |

author: Ian Sample Science editor
description:
A mile beneath the Black Hills, scientists are building giant detectors to analyse neutrino particles – and possibly find the answer to existence

For more than a century, the mining town of Lead, in the Black Hills of South Dakota, attracted workers with a taste for gold. Now, a flagship experiment being built in the old mine is drawing scientists in search of more intriguing riches: answers to the deepest mysteries of the universe.

Construction of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (Dune) in the former Homestake mine is due to start on Monday. Engineers will begin assembling four giant detectors inside caverns blasted from rock a mile underground.

Continue reading...
title: From gold rush to cosmic questions: a South Dakota mine and the search for the secrets of the universe

author: Kevin Rawlinson
description:
Defence secretary says value for money and modernisation key for spending to ‘fight the wars ahead’

The defence secretary, Wes Streeting, says he started stockpiling food and water weeks ago in case of a national emergency, as he talked up the threats to the UK and said his department had already begun ramping up its spending in response.

Streeting spoke after the chancellor, John Healey, said he wanted defence spending to reach 3% of GDP by 2030 and 3.5% by 2035; having already asked Whitehall departments to find 1% cuts in their budgets for long-term investment to fund defence spending.

Continue reading...
title: Streeting says he began stockpiling food weeks ago amid rising threat to UK

author: Natricia Duncan in Montego Bay and Anthony Lugg; photographs by Ina Sotirova
description:
A temporary injunction in the coastline battle for beaches to be publicly accessible, not sealed off for private developments, is just a step in fighting what islanders call a tourism model that disadvantages Jamaicans

When the Australian human rights lawyer Eva Buzo emerged from the sea on to the shores of One Man Beach in Montego Bay on Sunday after her gruelling, nearly 11-hour-long swim, the thunderous pulse of welcome drums was drowned out by the chants of “free beach” from jubilant supporters.

Here in Jamaica’s tourism capital, against a backdrop of jagged mountains and sunset-tinted clouds, Buzo – a celebrated marathon swimmer – said she was pleased to help support the important work of the Jamaica Beach Birthright Environmental Movement (Jabbem) and others fighting for free public access to Jamaica’s beaches.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Plantation tourism’: court victory signals hope in Jamaica’s fight to keep beaches public

author: Nick Robins-Early, Andrew Witherspoon, Will Craft, Alvaro Dominguez, and Daniel Wolfe
description:
The tech mogul’s midterm donations backing Republicans have made him the largest single-cycle political donor in modern US history

Elon Musk has poured so much money into US politics this midterms election cycle that his donations could fund half a dozen SpaceX rocket launches or buy thousands of Tesla Cybertrucks. At the Tesla Diner in Los Angeles, Musk could order more than 31.9m cheeseburgers with the money he has spent on the midterms.

Musk, the world’s richest person, has funnelled at least $445.77m into Republican-aligned political action committees (Pacs) and groups since last year, according to US Federal Election Commission data as of 29 October. The contributions have made him the Republicans’ most prominent financial backer and the largest single-cycle political donor in modern US history.
title: The staggering $446m Elon Musk has spent on the US midterms – visualized

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Strand magazine to feature never-before-seen article from Hungarian-born escapologist who was also a prolific author

Unseen writing by Harry Houdini, the world’s most renowned escapologist and illusionist, is being published in the US on Saturday, the 100th anniversary of his death.

As well as being famous for his magic acts and quest to expose fake mediums and spiritualists before he died in 1926 at the age of 52, Houdini, whose real name was Eric Weisz, was a prolific author, with more than two dozen books, short stories and plays to his name.

Continue reading...
title: Unseen Harry Houdini writing published on 100th anniversary of his death

Tonight’s referee is NRL veteran Ashley Klein.

3rd over: Australia 14-2 (Head 9, Green 1) Brave of Green to leave the ball outside off. Similar spot to the one that got Marnus, a touch fuller perhaps. He gets moving from the fifth ball, knocks a single into the off side.

Two boundaries, but if I were South Africa, I’d happily feed that shot a few times looking for th
title: South Africa v Australia: third men’s cricket Test, day five – live

author: Billy Munday
description:
⚽ All the latest as we build up to Saturday’s games
⚽ Ten things to look out for | Fixtures | Mail Billy

“It’s not always rosy and nice conversations,” Michael Carrick said on Thursday as he reflected on a difficult week at United amid speculation over his future and the general state of the club.

United have gone eight games without a win after their worst league start in 40 years. They are 16th in the Premier League, one point above the relegation zone. Carrick suggested he had held talks with Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada this week …

It’s pretty clear, it’s not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone, whether that’s between me and the players, whether that’s between me, Jason, Omar or the owners.
title: Chelsea v Manchester United buildup, Premier League, WSL and more – matchday live

author: Emma Brockes
description:
Her unsparing fiction and true crime writing have made her one of Australia’s most controversial and celebrated authors. The author discusses relationships, resilience – and finding global recognition five decades into her career

A few years ago, when Helen Garner had an idea to write a book about Australian rules football, her heart soared then immediately sank. The impetus was Ambrose, her teenage grandson, who played for a local team. Garner enjoyed watching them and wanted to put this into writing. Then the dreary thought: “I’ll have to swot, read the rulebook.” People to whom she mentioned the idea assumed she’d be writing a polemic, “like what it means in society and how terrible it is and what violence means. And I’m going: ‘What a bore.’”

As anyone familiar with Garner’s almost 50-year writing career will know, there is nothing more igniting to the 83-year-old than the invitation to outrun boredom by going off in an unauthorised direction. Garner, who is sp
title: ‘Being hated is very bracing’: Helen Garner on surviving three marriages and being called a ‘rotten feminist’

author: Andrew Lawrence
description:
In a revealing documentary, a looksmaxxing-influenced world where ‘your social capital is tied to your appearance’ has led to more men wanting more

Man’s obsession with his member is a tale as old as time, writ large in sky-scraping edifices, in allusions that flatter (big dick energy) or offend (prick), in the countless artifacts across the ages that venerate male potency – a porn star’s description of Donald Trump’s “toadstool” penis. But it’s the booming intimate wellness industry – AKA the rash (ahem) of fillers, therapies and cosmetic procedures that have come into vogue since the little blue pill rocked the market – that most intrigued Daniel Lombroso, the esteemed documentarian who made his name at the Atlantic and the New Yorker dissecting male fragility.

“A lot of the stories I worked on at those places were kind of fringy subculture and oftentimes adjacent to white nationalism,” says Lombroso, who became aware of the rising demand for penile enhancement proced
title: ‘Never big enough’: inside the booming penis enlargement industry

author: Patrick Greenfield
description:
Cop17, focused on protecting nature and restoring ecosystems, concludes on Saturday with critics saying system allows ‘one idiot’ to stall progress

Calls are growing for major reforms to UN biodiversity summits as countries fail to deliver on their promises to halt the destruction of the natural world, with governments likely on track to continue their record of never having met a target in the 34-year history of the convention.

Two weeks of negotiations at biodiversity Cop17 in Yerevan, Armenia, concluded on Saturday morning with countries vowing to redouble their efforts to meeting this decade’s targets, which include commitments to protect 30% of the planet for nature, restore nearly a third of Earth’s degraded ecosystems and reform $500bn (£410bn) of environmentally damaging subsidies.
title: ‘Bunch of baloney’: calls grow for Cop summit reforms as latest event on track to fail targets

author: Presented by Aditya Chakrabortty with Karel Williams and Sukhdev Johal, produced by Frankie Tobi and Luke John Smith , the executive producers are Maz Ebtehaj, Kirsty Major and James Tindale
description:
What if someone told you the truth about the economy? For years, UK governments have tried spending more, spending less, cutting red tape, leaving the EU, levelling up, and they have still failed to increase growth per person. So what’s the lesson from the great British fairytale? On the latest episode, the rebel economists Karel Williams and Sukhdev Johal explain to Aditya Chakrabortty why they believe praying for growth is a fool’s dream – and why it won’t improve your life

Aditya’s suggested reading list for Karel Williams and Sukhdev Johal:

As we say in the podcast, I’ve championed the work of Karel and Sukhdev and their colleagues in the Guardian for many years, and some of my columns are a good introduction to their approach.

• In our conversation we look at what life after growth looks like for towns and suburbs, and what it should look like.
title: Why politicians chasing economic growth is a lie | Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty

author: Gwilym Mumford
description:
In this week’s newsletter: Sandra Hüller and Anne Hathaway might have been in more films this year – but Pattinson’s remarkable run confirms him as one of the best performers of his generation

For prolific actors, 2026 has been a banner year. The roles have kept piling up for a small cohort of stars, the roles have kept piling up, to the point where you wonder how they found the time to do vital things like sleep, shower or scarf down nuclear-fallout-covered chicken wings on YouTube interview shows.

Just look at Sandra Hüller, who by the time December ends will have racked up six projects in 2026, ranging from austere cold war road-trip movies to migraine-inducing Marvel blockbusters. Anne Hathaway, meanwhile, has since January appeared as – deep breath – a psychologically tormented fading pop star, a catatonic
title: The Guide #267: Robert Pattinson embraced his inner low life and became one of the best actors of his era

author: Rhik Samadder
description:
Heated Rivalry’s Hudson Williams and Carrie-Anne Moss star in this audacious mystery about a Slavic witch. There’s supernatural weirdness, detective work … and a hero who looks a lot like Tim Key dressed in leather

Halloween was once a simpler time, when neighbourhood kids would dress up as mythical serial killers, the undead or bedsheet-wearing ghosts. At some point, following America’s lead, it became sexy and cat-forward. It has now become a sort of conceptual art show. I’ve heard people this year planning to go to parties dressed as Erling Haaland, Prom Carrie (Prime Video edition) and Bad Bunny’s half-time Super Bowl show. It’s horrifying.

The perception of witches has evolved, too. Once understood to be a malignant version of the crone archetype, sympathy for witches has grown. They have been embraced as a feminist image of the older woman, free of patriarchal command and possessed of a powerful rage. In recent years, Maleficent, Elphaba from Wicked and Mar
title: Yaga: chicken bones? Saltburn parties? This folk horror is so debauched, it’s hilarious

author: Martin Pegan
description:
• Joanna Wietrzyk claims victory in first event of season in Hamburg

  • Australian says pre-race that she is ‘truly so sorry’ for events in Beijing

The Australian athlete who sparked outrage when winning a Hyrox event in Beijing despite soiling herself during the race has returned in style with victory in the first event of the new season in Hamburg.

Joanna Wietrzyk won the endurance sports event in China last month but forfeited the points and soon faced a stinging public backlash as footage of her continuing through demanding exercises and using communal equipment with faecal matter running down her legs went viral on social media.

Continue reading...
title: Hyrox athlete who soiled herself puts ‘confronting’ matter behind her to win return race

description:
Nelson, 41, who works in legal services, meets Louise, 37, who works in marketing

What were you hoping for?
Great company and wonderful conversation.

title: Blind date: ‘He said: “If heaven is real, you’ll definitely be going there”, which might be the nicest thing anyone’s ever said to me’

author: Hugh Muir
description:
There is always debate about the concept’s necessity and efficacy. But with nativists in their pomp, it’s good to focus on who we are and why

  • What forces shaped four generations of Black Britons? | The panel

Pity Black History Month UK, assailed on all sides. Those on the right seek to end the celebration on the basis that it amounts to special treatment for a group that doesn’t deserve it. History should be colour-blind: society should not differentiate, they say. We are not racist, we just want fairness. But often, they are – and they really don’t.

On the other side of the argument are the progressives, notably minority progressives, who say the idea of a month to consider Black history is demeaning because it should already have a year-round place in our teaching and consciousness. There
title: When you’re traduced, abused and gaslighted – believe me, Black History Month matters  | Hugh Muir

author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent and Neil Marks in Georgetown
description:
Activists see meeting as opportunity to demand UK confront role in transatlantic enslavement

“The royal family enslaved us! Apologise now! Reparatory justice now!”

King Charles and the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, will be greeted with messages as they travel through Antigua’s capital, St John’s, to attend meetings at the Commonwealth leaders’ summit next week. On billboards, placards and T-shirts, in letters and at a candlelight vigil for the thousands of Africans trafficked to Antigua and Barbuda during the transatlantic slave trade, the message from the Caribbean will be pervasive: slavery reparations is not an issue they “are going to be able to dodge”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Reparations now’: King and Burnham face protests at Antigua Commonwealth summit

author: Tim Dowling
description:
My wife got ours when she was eight, and he came to live with us soon after we got married. I don’t remember anything about that in the vows

It is the first truly bleak day of autumn – the sky is a deep grey and a steady drizzle is falling. Sitting in the unflattering light of a kitchen downlight and looking out the window, I think: this is it now, until spring.

Except it isn’t, quite, as a few hours later the cloud begins to break up and a shaft of watery sunlight reaches the brick step just outside my office shed. When I open the door to let in the warm afternoon air, I find the tortoise sitting there.

Continue reading...
title: Tim Dowling: having a tortoise reminds you that life is long

description:
Tom Kerridge, Helen Goh and other foodies on what they feed their children

Acey, 10

Continue reading...
title: Don’t make sugar a treat –or hide the broccoli: top chefs on how to make your kids happy eaters

author: George Francis Lee
description:
One south London bar provided Claudia Winkleman-themed cocktails and its very own banishment ceremony

Cries, cheers and boos emanating from pubs across the country on Friday night were less likely to be linked to any sports fixture than the nation coming together for the dramatic climax of the BBC’s The Celebrity Traitors.

The cloak and dagger reality show, in which contestants attempt to deceive or deduce who among them are “Faithfuls” and “Traitors” for a charity cash prize, drew in more than half of the UK’s TV audience in its debut episode earlier this month.

Continue reading...
title: ‘They cheer like it’s football’: Celebrity Traitors fans hit bars to watch climax

author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
description:
Consultation follows growing calls from campaigners, vets and National Farmers’ Union for tighter regulation

As the nights draw in, the season of sparklers begins, with Diwali, Bonfire Night and New Year’s Eve among the occasions typically celebrated with fireworks. But if campaigners get their way, this could be the last blast for bangers in the back yard.

In January concerns about the noise and availability of fireworks were aired in a parliamentary debate, with two petitions clocking up more than 180,000 signatures each, while earlier this month the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade closed a consultation on proposals including making louder fireworks only
title: Is time up for backyard fireworks? UK ministers weigh partial ban over noise concerns

author: Emma Beddington
description:
In a survey, ‘just to be clear’ came out as the most loathed phrase. But I think I can do better

A new contender for the most passive-aggressive email phrase has emerged. “Just to be clear” was chosen by 52% of desk jockeys in a survey by email verification company ZeroBounce, closely followed by the perennial pass-ag fave, “per my last email” (40%), which tied with the identical-in-intent “as previously discussed”. Further down the list came “for future reference” and “kindly note”.

If you ask me, these all verge on actual aggressive. Imagine saying “just to be clear” out loud to another person: that’s a conversational poke in the ribs, isn’t it? It’s the kind of thing you unleash 10 minutes into an ill-tempered wrangle with your home insurance company about inflated renewal premiums. “Kindly note” is even worse – it’s a phrase from an angry message on the office kitchen wall about microwave abuse.
title: ‘Apologies for any confusion!’: how to write the perfect passive-aggressive email

author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Azzarnug
description:
With 180,000 eligible voters, Bedouin turnout was key in Palestinian-led parties winning unprecedented 19 seats

Last year, Umm Khaled Fatoum returned from volunteering in a Jewish-Arab support centre for victims of war to find bulldozers tearing into her son’s house in the Bedouin village of Azzarnug.

The demolition crew, who arrived under police escort, did not even allow them to remove furniture or solar panels before reducing the home and its contents to a pile of rubble.

Continue reading...
title: ‘You need the power of all your votes’: Bedouin women secure success for Arab parties in Israeli election

author: Victoria Bekiempis
description:
Mangione pleaded guilty in August in federal case in the killing of UnitedHealthcare executive Brian Thompson

Luigi Mangione’s lawyers filed paperwork on Friday once again pushing for dismissal of his state-level case in the killing of UnitedHealthcare executive Brian Thompson following his federal guilty plea.

Mangione pleaded guilty on 14 August to federal charges in Thompson’s grisly death outside a Manhattan hotel on 4 December 2024. The shocking plea came less than a month before his state murder and weapons trial, which had been scheduled for 8 September.

Continue reading...
title: Luigi Mangione’s lawyers file to dismiss state charges, citing double jeopardy law

author: Oliver Holmes in Bangkok, Daniel Boffey in London and Adeshola Ore in Melbourne
description:
The MV Odyssey was billed as the ultimate escape from Donald Trump. Instead, the oil shock caused by his war has left passengers unceremoniously dumped in Cambodia

The idea was a never-ending retirement at sea, a continuous voyage around the globe. The promise to the passengers of the MV Odyssey cruise ship – many approaching the autumn of their lives – was that on the open seas they could cut loose from the troubles of the world. But the world had other ideas.

The end came in an announcement as stark as it was brief: they had seven hours to get off. They were going no further than Cambodia.

Continue reading...
title: The cursed cruise: how the dream of never-ending luxury at sea became a nightmare

author: Romita Saluja in Delhi
description:
On a wildlife walk in the Indian capital, a group of women share their stories of trying to enjoy nature in a city where strangers feel entitled to harass them

Vallari Sheel wishes she could carry a camera or a pair of binoculars without being asked what her father does for a living. Once, looking at a tree in her south Delhi neighbourhood, about 50 metres away from her home, a man in a car screamed at her: “You have been clicking photos here for 10 days. What are you going to do with them?”

Sheel, an urban ecologist, spends hours observing trees of all types in all seasons. She often travels by car for her own safety, worries about the impact of her work on her family, and has clear guidance for her female interns when they are, inevitably, approached: don’t engage, don’t respond.

C
title: ‘Don’t worry about the leopard. It’s a man you don’t want to run into’: Delhi women reclaim the outdoors

After attempt at acquittal or retrial was dismissed, Patterson has 28 days to lodge an application for special leave to appeal to Australia’s high court

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

After losing her bid for a retrial, the mushroom murderer Erin Patterson could take her fight to the highest court in Australia.

But her prospects of success are far from rosy, a legal expert says.

title: Will mushroom murderer Erin Patterson make a final bid for freedom and what are the prospects of a high court appeal?

author: Associated Press
description:
Order says local officials can’t be forced to separate or stop counting ballots that the government deems to be disputed

A federal judge has barred the justice department from threatening or coercing election workers to stop processing ballots.

The order issued late Friday also bars the justice department from demanding local election officials segregate or not count ballots that the federal government deems may have been cast by ineligible voters.

Continue reading...
title: Federal judge bars DoJ from threatening election workers to stop processing ballots

author: Ben Doherty and Associated Press
description:
Marco Rubio pulls plug on traditional photo op at meeting of foreign ministers after about one-third of countries threaten boycott

The traditional “family photo” to open the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting has been abruptly cancelled in the US after a host of nations – including Australia and the UK – refused to appear beside Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov.

US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, pulled the plug after several European officials, the UK and Australia made it known they would boycott or walk out of the snapshot that often kicks off such international gatherings.

Continue reading...
title: US cancels G20 ‘family photo’ after Australia, UK and others refuse to appear with Russia

author: Eva Corlett in Auckland
description:
When the Guardian visited the Maungakiekie electorate, two themes emerge: a grudging fealty to the National party and growing support for minor parties

It’s a hot spring day in the Auckland suburb of Onehunga, and the main strip is starting to hum with life. Builders slip into a bakery for a snack, retirees chat over coffee outside cafes and a shoeless man zips by on a scooter.

There are few signs New Zealand’s general election is looming along this shopping strip but Onehunga and neighbouring suburbs that make up the electorate Maungakiekie, will be closely watched when New Zealand heads to the polls on 7 November.

Continue reading...
title: In New Zealand’s bellwether seat, what are locals thinking as a knife-edge poll looms?

author: Yu-chen Li in Taipei
description:
The rounding up of customers at a gay bar weeks before Saturday’s Pride festival has some questioning the island’s progressive image

Josh was having a drink at Commander D, a popular gay bar in Taipei, on a Saturday afternoon when several police officers suddenly burst in. “Squat down and don’t move,” they shouted. Bewildered, he looked around to see the bar owner being handcuffed and forced to his knees.

The 28-year-old was among 51 customers to be rounded up and taken away for questioning over suspected breaches of public decency rules.

Continue reading...
title: ‘We’re not freaks’: police raid sparks concern for Taiwan’s LGBT-friendly image
